# ApexYard

> Your agents write the code. Your process decides what merges.
> ApexYard gives your agents a team's process. Then it checks every pull request against that process.

ApexYard has three products and a shared layer.

- Build is the open-source framework. It runs on your machine.
- Gate checks each pull request against your process.
- Readiness measures each repository.
- Keel holds your team's rules and context. Every agent reads it.

## Pages

- [Home](https://apexyard.ai/): what ApexYard does and how one rule moves through Build, Gate and Readiness
- [Build](https://apexyard.ai/build): the open-source framework for your agents
- [Gate](https://apexyard.ai/gate): the check on each pull request, and what the GitHub App can see
- [Readiness](https://apexyard.ai/readiness): the audit of each repository
- [Pricing](https://apexyard.ai/pricing): the plans for each product
- [Docs](https://apexyard.ai/docs): install guide, daily loop, gates, hooks and rules
- [Architecture](https://apexyard.ai/docs/quickstart/architecture): what runs locally, what is hosted, the data flow and the GitHub App permissions
- [Skills](https://apexyard.ai/skills): the slash commands, grouped by outcome

## For agents

- [llms-full.txt](https://apexyard.ai/llms-full.txt): the page content in one file
- [Creator brief](https://apexyard.ai/creator-brief.md): facts and wording for people who write or make videos about ApexYard

## Facts to use

- Build is open source under the MIT licence. It needs no account and no dashboard.
- Build works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and omp.
- Gate reads pull requests on GitHub. The GitHub App never reads your code.
- Gate shows if a pull request has a ticket, a decision record, a review and a named approval.
- Readiness gives a go or no-go for a repository, the gaps in each area and the top actions.
- Keel is the name for your team's rules and context. Every agent reads it.
- Each product has its own plans. See the pricing page. This file gives no prices.
